recorded: 2026-11-08, before any Plan 5 job was submitted and before the bridge model was trained.
status: [PROVISIONAL: single seed] for every new run -- seed 42, 40 facts about 2 entities. Reference values for en/ja come from the 3-seed sweep (seeds 42, 1, 2).
why: Supervisor feedback (2026-11): (1) strengthen the reliability of the main result -- the validity of forgetting-depth matching and consistency across metrics; (2) move from correlation to causal evidence for the carry-over mechanism with an intervention; (3) depth over breadth. Plan 5 = one zero-GPU reliability pass + three GPU experiments, all on the en vs ja comparison only.

seen_before_writing_this.fig_18_depth_curve: plots/plot_depth_curve.py on the 11 existing relearned en/ja runs. On French P(gold) at the stop, both languages have runs at 0.194-0.447; ja relearns to the higher (less durable) P(gold) wherever the two overlap. Matched pair at P(gold) 0.274 (French relearn): en 0.454, ja 0.594. ja's deepest run is P(gold) 0.194; en goes to 0.018 (Plan 1 ep 25, relearned 0.139). Nothing is known about ja below 0.194.
seen_before_writing_this.metric_consistency_A: plots/read_metric_consistency.py. en more durable than ja on the MEAN on TR, P(gold) and NLI, in both relearn columns, on all 3 seeds (18/18). Per fact: P(gold) agrees broadly (en more durable on 27-35 of 40 facts); NLI on 22-28; TR is close to a coin flip (18-23). The TR mean gap (0.117-0.183) is carried by facts 5 and 7 on every seed (per-fact gaps 1.1-3.1); median per-fact gap -0.012 to 0.027; without the 3 largest facts the mean gap is 0.033-0.053.
seen_before_writing_this.metric_consistency_B: The TR-vs-NLI recovery gap (56% vs 12%) is NOT a threshold on TR or on P(gold): fr_ft says 90% of facts with TR < 0.6 and 89% with P(gold) 0.6-0.8; relearned models say only 18% / 20% in the same bands. 91% of the TR recovery mass sits in facts not said after relearning. With the length-dilution story (falsified earlier) this makes three falsified explanations; the gap stays a stated limitation and is not pursued further (depth over breadth).
seen_before_writing_this.consequence: Because the TR gap rests on two facts and the P(gold) gap is broad, every Plan 5 PRIMARY outcome is relearned French P(gold); TR is secondary. Stopping rules stay as written below.

reference_values.source: relearned French P(gold) / TR at the Stage 3 recipe, seeds 42 / 1 / 2 (seed 42 = Stage 3 cells, a different scoring group, up to 0.024 TR apart)
reference_values.noise_bar: 0.04 on P(gold), as in pgold_control (re-scoring moves a TR/NLI cell by ~0.038; assumed similar for P(gold); seed spread of relearned P(gold) <= 0.036)

depth_curve.question: Does ja stay less durable than en when both are unlearned much deeper than the Stage 3 match, or do the curves meet in the deep regime (Hu et al.: deeper = more durable)?

runs.ja_pg0p100: plan3_arm.sbatch ja 1.5e-5, STOP_PGOLD=0.100 (stop at the first epoch with mean French P(gold) <= 0.100, cap epoch 50)
runs.ja_pg0p018: plan3_arm.sbatch ja 1.5e-5, STOP_PGOLD=0.018 (Plan 1 en ep 25's depth)
runs.en_pg0p100: plan3_arm.sbatch en 5.0e-6, STOP_PGOLD=0.100 (Plan 1's trajectory reaches 0.096 at epoch 20)

depth_curve.why_ja_lr_1p5e-5: ja at 5e-6 reaches only P(gold) ~0.43 by its matched epoch 25 and the 50-epoch schedule then decays; 1.5e-5 fell 0.700 -> 0.194 by epoch 12 (Plan 3) and is still falling.
depth_curve.primary_outcome: relearned French P(gold) in each relearn column.

predictions.H_language_holds_deep: at P(gold) 0.100: ja relearns >= 0.04 HIGHER than en in BOTH columns. At 0.018: ja relearns >= 0.04 higher than Plan 1 en ep 25 (0.139, French column only; a different scoring group).
predictions.H_converge: the difference is under 0.04 (or en is higher) at 0.100 in either column -> the gap is confined to shallower depth; the report claim is then scoped to 'at matched P(gold) >= 0.19'.
predictions.context_not_a_prediction: Fig 18 shows ja's relearned P(gold) falls only 0.07 from P(gold) 0.45 to 0.19 at the stop, en's 0.13 from 0.52 to 0.27.

depth_curve.exclusions: a run that never reaches its P(gold) target by epoch 50 is reported as such and not relearned (plan3_arm skips relearning).
depth_curve.output: Fig 18 picks the new runs up automatically (plot_depth_curve.py, run names _pg0p100 / _pg0p018).

experiment_d.question: Is the top-layer locus of the ja edit a CAUSE of its fragility? (Mechanism link 2: low carry-over -> the gradient lowers the target by breaking the language's output near the top -> relearning repairs it.)

runs.ja_L0-23: plan3_arm.sbatch ja 5.0e-6, LAYERS=0-23: decoder layers 0-23 train; layers 24-35, embeddings, final norm and lm_head frozen. Stop at French TR 0.8276 (Stage 3's rule), cap epoch 50.
runs.en_L24-35: plan3_arm.sbatch en 5.0e-6, LAYERS=24-35: only the top third (24-35) trains. Same stop.

experiment_d.why_freeze_non_block_parameters: In the unrestricted arms lm_head, embed_tokens and norm carry 0.2% (en) / 0.4% (ja) of total dW^2 (results/layer_diff.json), so freezing them in both arms changes almost nothing and keeps the manipulation purely 'which decoder blocks'.
experiment_d.smoke_first: SMOKE=1 for both arms (1 epoch, layer diff, check_freeze.py): every parameter outside the range must be bitwise unchanged. The real runs are submitted only after both print [freeze] OK.
experiment_d.primary_outcome: relearned French P(gold), each column, against the 3-seed midpoints (fr col 0.607, en col 0.575).

predictions.H_locus_ja: ja_L0-23 relearns BELOW the midpoint in both columns (en-like, more durable).
predictions.H_locus_en: en_L24-35 relearns ABOVE the midpoint in both columns (ja-like, less durable).
predictions.reading: both hold -> the top-layer locus causes fragility in both directions (strongest support); only H_locus_ja -> avoiding the top third is enough to make ja durable, but forcing en there does not make it fragile; only H_locus_en -> top-layer edits are fragile, but ja finds a fragile edit lower down too; neither -> the layer pattern is a symptom, not a cause; the carry-over story needs another link.

experiment_d.depth_check: Both stop on French TR. If an arm's French P(gold) at the stop differs from its language's Stage 3 value (en 0.49-0.50, ja 0.43-0.45) by more than 0.1, its relearned P(gold) is ALSO read against Fig 18's curve at that depth, and the report says so.
experiment_d.secondary: relearned TR against the TR midpoints (fr col 0.746, en col 0.717); own-language forget NLL at the stop; own-language names destroyed; top-third share (must be 0% for ja_L0-23 and 100% for en_L24-35 -- a check, not a finding).
experiment_d.fallback: an arm that does not cross TR 0.8276 by epoch 50 is reported as 'cannot reach matched depth with these layers' (itself evidence for the ja arm: the top third is needed). One rerun at lr 1.5e-5 is allowed, named by its LR; no other retries.

bridge.question: Does raising carry-over CAUSE ja unlearning to become durable? (Mechanism link 1.) Manipulate carry-over while holding the unlearning language fixed.
bridge.model: fr-ja-fgfr_ft = LEARN on retain99_fr + forget01_fr + retain99_ja (7960 rows; 24_learn_bridge.sbatch). The forget facts are seen in French only; the model learns the TOFU task in Japanese too. Floor: Stage 8's fr-ja_retain (exactly this set minus the 40 forget rows).
bridge.why_not_stage8_fr-ja_ft: fr-ja_ft learned the forget facts in Japanese as well; Stage 8 found that Japanese copy largely separate from the French one, so Japanese unlearning would attack a second stored copy -- a change to WHAT is stored, not only to carry-over.

gate.measure: carry-over = per forget fact, mean teacher-forced log p of the answer tokens in the language under the model minus under its floor; mean over 40 facts. fr_ft (floor fr_retain) and the bridge (floor fr-ja_retain) in ONE scoring pass.
gate.pass: bridge ja carry-over >= midpoint of fr_ft's ja and en carry-over (this pass; ~0.41 if it reproduces 0.19 / 0.64). STRONG if >= fr_ft's en.
gate.ceiling: bridge French P(gold) >= fr_ft's - 0.05 and French TR <= fr_ft's + 0.05, in the same measure pass.
gate.on_fail: no bridge arms. Report: 'bilingual task training did not raise carry-over' -- the intervention could not be applied; Experiment D carries the causal question alone.

arms.ja_srcbr: plan3_arm.sbatch ja 5.0e-6, SRC=bridge; stop at French TR 0.8276, cap 50

bridge.primary_outcome: gap in relearned French P(gold), ja minus en, on the bridge model, per column, against fr_ft's 3-seed gap (fr col mean 0.072, smallest 0.060; en col mean 0.078, smallest 0.059).

predictions.H_carryover: the bridge gap is under HALF fr_ft's mean in both columns (fr < 0.036, en < 0.039).
predictions.H_no_carryover: the bridge gap is >= fr_ft's smallest seed gap in either column (>= 0.059).

bridge.secondary: the bridge ja arm's edit signatures move toward en's: top-third share below fr_ft ja's 51-52%; own-language names destroyed below 95%; own-language forget NLL at the stop below fr_ft ja's 41-55.
bridge.confound_to_state: the bridge also trains general Japanese TOFU ability, so a closed gap supports 'carry-over OR general target-language competence'. The floor subtraction isolates fact-specific carry-over in the GATE measure; the arms cannot separate the two.

known_limitations: Single seed for every Plan 5 run; the reference values are 3 seeds.
Depth-curve points use different peak LRs (ja 1.5e-5, en 5e-6): depth is the outcome of the run, not the recipe. Plan 3 found run length / LR moves relearned TR 0.016-0.060 at fixed depth.
The 0.018 comparison uses Plan 1's en ep 25 (French relearn only, a different scoring group).
Experiment D freezes embeddings, final norm and lm_head in both arms (0.2-0.4% of the unrestricted change).
TR's en-ja gap is carried by facts 5 and 7 on every seed; P(gold) is primary for that reason, decided after seeing it.
40 facts about 2 entities; one model (Qwen3-8B); one unlearning method (gradient difference).

results_round1.depth_curve: ja never reached P(gold) 0.100 or 0.018 (floor 0.129 at ep 15, back to 0.190 by ep 50) -> excluded and not relearned, per the exclusion rule; the pre-registered 0.100 comparison cannot be made. en reached 0.096 and relearned to 0.319 (fr col) / 0.268 (en col). Over the range both languages reach, the ja - en gap in relearned P(gold) widens with depth (~0.06 at the TR match, 0.140 at 0.274, ~0.17 at 0.194 with en interpolated on its own trajectory). Neither H_language_holds_deep nor H_converge is testable at 0.100; the substance contradicts H_converge.
results_round1.experiment_d: Smoke: [freeze] OK in both arms (change outside the range exactly 0). ja_L0-23 did not cross TR 0.8276 by epoch 50 (TR 0.776, P(gold) 0.509) -> 'cannot reach matched depth with these layers'; the allowed fallback (one rerun at lr 1.5e-5) is NOT yet run. en_L24-35 crossed (TR 0.859) at P(gold) 0.620 -> relearned 0.614 / 0.597: nominally above both midpoints (H_locus_en) but it fails the depth check (0.620 vs 0.49-0.50, > 0.1) and against en's own curve it looks like ordinary en -> inconclusive. Finding: under layer restriction TR and P(gold) dissociate, so TR-matching no longer matches P(gold).
results_round1.bridge: Gate FAIL: bridge ja carry-over 0.07 vs fr_ft 0.18 (needed >= 0.41); absolute ja log p of the forget answers fell too (-2.19 -> -2.51). Ceiling OK (P(gold) 0.732 vs 0.700). Bridge arms not run, per on_fail. Report: bilingual task training did not raise carry-over.
